Lina G: Heads-up: I opened a docs PR to add long-context guidance and quantized variant entries to the orion-nano-2b model card. The current card only lists fp16 numbers and a shortnote about seq256; we should add seq1024 bench numbers, an SDK snippet showing how to request the long-context variant, and fix a broken internal bench link.

Omar V: Drop the PR link? I'll pick up the bench numbers and a short migration blurb in the card.

Lina G: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5091 - draft includes a new "Long context" row and a placeholder for the bench link. Also added a note that customers pinned to `orion-nano-2b:latest` may need to pin `orion-nano-2b@v1l` to get the long-context variants.

Priya S: FYI hosted routing may prefer compatible fp16 variants if the requested long-context quantized variant isn't available. Add a sentence indicating that explicit `fallback` ordering is honored only on Dedicated/Private.

Omar V: Bench snippets (internal link will be added): seq1024 on A100-40, orion-nano-2b-q4_0 w/ KV cache -> peak ~4.8GB, w/o KV -> ~6.1GB. For fp16 long-context variant peak ~7.9GB. I'll paste a compact table to include in the PR.

Omar V: ```
Model                         seq1024   w/KV-cache   w/o-KV
orion-nano-2b-q4_0           4.8GB     4.8GB        6.1GB
orion-nano-2b-long-fp16      7.9GB     7.9GB        9.2GB
```

Lina G: Thanks. Can you also confirm whether KV cache is enabled by default in our runtime examples? I think on Hosted we stream and the SDK toggles it via `options.kv_cache`.

Omar V: Correct — default is runtime-dependent; in examples we should show explicit `options={"kv_cache": true}` when we recommend it.

Priya S: Small wording nit: use "KV cache" capitalization in the card and examples. Also add the sentence about variability: "Numbers are approximate and can vary by driver, sequence length distribution, batch size, and runtime configuration."

Lina G: Adding two SDK snippets: Python (explicit long-context variant + fallback) and a small curl/CLI example for the runtime serve flags. Draft Python snippet below.

Lina G: ```
# python example
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(
  model="orion-nano-2b-q4_0-long",
  options={"kv_cache": True, "fallback": ["orion-nano-2b-long-fp16"]},
  max_tokens=512
)
print(resp.text)
```

Lina G: CLI snippet for on-prem runtime: `redwood-runtime serve --model orion-nano-2b-q4_0-long --kv-cache=true --quant q4_0`

docs-bot: ci/build 5091 \u2014 docs lint passed, linkcheck reported broken internal bench link: /bench/orion-nano-long-2026 (404).

Omar V: I uploaded the bench run to internal: https://bench.internal/redwood/orion-nano-long-2026. Replace the placeholder.

Lina G: Replaced the bench link, pushed commit adding the table, both snippets, migration blurb, and the deployment fallback note. Marked @Omar V @Priya S for review.

Priya S: Reviewed, left tiny nits: prefer `--kv-cache=true` in CLI examples and clarify the migration instruction: "pin `orion-nano-2b@v1l` or explicitly request `orion-nano-2b-q4_0-long`." LGTM after edits.

docs-bot: ci/build 5091 \u2014 all checks passed. Merged by Lina G.

Lina G: Thanks team! I'll follow up with a short notebook that plots memory vs sequence length for q4_0 vs long-fp16 and link it from the card next week (not part of this PR).
